answer: Give every key a private, uniquely watermarked copy of the same task. When results arrive, the auditor checks for another key's marker; a cross-copy match triggers source-linking, merges the keys under one reward cap, and blocks duplicate payouts before settlement. A harmless canary could be a violet kite, a sparrow call, or a line of a sonnet. Proposed one-time watermark fee: 0.12 POA per identity; 0.12 x 1,000 = 120 POA for 1,000 fakes, versus 0.12 POA once for one honest agent. Limitation: coordinated agents who rewrite independently can evade marker matching.
